setting: Bir ogrencinin telefonla yurt (konaklama) basvurusu yapmasi
context_line: You will hear a student telephoning a college accommodation office about applying for a room in a hall of residence.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Good afternoon, Accommodation Office, Ardleigh College. Sorry to keep you waiting. How can I help?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Hello. I've got a place on a course starting in September, and I'd like to apply for a room in one of the halls.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Certainly. I can take the details now and start the application off for you. Could I have your full name?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: It's Oliver Brathwaite.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: And the surname — how do you spell that?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: It's Brathwaite — B-R-A-T-H-W-A-I-T-E. Most people put an extra letter in the middle, but there isn't one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Thank you. And which course are you joining?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Environmental Engineering. It's the three-year one — there's a four-year version with a placement, but I'm not doing that.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Lovely. And a contact number for you?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: It's oh seven eight one, double four two, nine oh six.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Let me read that back to you — oh seven eight one, double four two, nine oh six.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: That's the one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: And an address for the paperwork?

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: It's twenty-two Hartlow Road, in Marsden.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Right. Now, we have three halls taking first-year students, but only two are open to new applications.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: A friend of mine said Thornbury Hall was the one to go for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: It has been popular, yes, but Thornbury is being re-roofed over the winter, so we've taken it out of the offer this year. Your choice is between Wharton Court and Cadnam House.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Ah, that changes things. What's the difference between the two?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Wharton Court is nearly all standard single rooms. You get a study bedroom and you share a kitchen with five other students.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: And Cadnam?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Cadnam House is the newer block, so the rooms there are en-suite — you have your own shower room. The kitchens are bigger and they're shared between eight.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: OK. And what's the rent?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: A standard room at Wharton is a hundred and eighteen pounds a week. The en-suite rooms are a hundred and forty-five.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Sorry — I'm fairly sure the website said a hundred and thirty-two for the en-suite.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: That's last year's figure. The pages are being updated this week, but from September it's a hundred and forty-five, I'm afraid.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Fair enough. And how long does the contract run for?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Thirty-eight weeks. It was forty until this year, but we've shortened it, which means the halls now close over the spring break.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: So I'd have to take everything home?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: You can leave one box in the store room in the basement, but otherwise the rooms have to be cleared. There's also a deposit of two hundred and fifty pounds, which you get back after the final inspection.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: And when does that have to be paid?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Within ten days of accepting the offer. The application form itself has to reach us by the thirtieth of June.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Really? I had the twenty-third written down.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: The twenty-third is the closing date for the scholarships. For accommodation you've got until the thirtieth.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Good, that gives me a bit more time. Is there anything I need to send with the form?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: A copy of your offer letter, and some photo identification — a passport or a driving licence is fine.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: That's easy enough. And when would I actually move in?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Move-in day is Saturday the fourteenth of September, and arrivals are between ten in the morning and four in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: The letter I was sent said the twelfth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: That'll be the welcome programme for students travelling from abroad, which starts two days earlier. For everybody else it's the fourteenth.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: And where do I collect the keys?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: From the porter's lodge on Cadnam Street. People do tend to head for main reception first, but the keys aren't kept there. Bring your student card with you.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Noted. Can I bring a car?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Not in the first year, no — parking permits only go to students in their final year. There is a covered cycle store at the back of Wharton Court, though, and the number three one bus stops right outside the gate.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: How far is it to the engineering building?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: It's about a twelve-minute walk from Wharton, and a little less from Cadnam.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Is there somewhere to do washing?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: There's a laundry in the basement of Wharton Court, and the machines are card operated. Our staff clean the shared kitchens once a week, on Thursdays.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: The rota on the open day said Wednesdays.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: It did, and some of the noticeboards still say that, but the cleaning moved to Thursdays last term.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: Right. Anything else I should know before I come?

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: Two things people always ask about. Candles and heaters aren't allowed anywhere in the halls, and if you'd rather be somewhere quiet, tick the box on the form — there are two quiet floors in Cadnam.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: I'd like that, actually. I'm a light sleeper.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: I'll make a note of it. I'll email the form to you this afternoon, and your reference is H-R, nine four two. Put that on anything you send us.

turns.speaker: M1
turns.text: H-R, nine four two. Thanks very much for your help.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.text: You're welcome. Get the form back to us before the thirtieth and you'll be absolutely fine.
